perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He is a project manager dealing with a project he believes is behind because his team seems unmotivated. He feels frustrated, anxious, at wit’s end, later hopeful/relieved, then disappointed/worried, then determined, optimistic, and empowered.
- He knows Arthur as a friend/advisor he can rely on for advice and support. He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- In their first meeting, Harold told Arthur that his team seemed unmotivated and that it was affecting project progress. He heard Arthur say motivation can be tricky, ask whether Harold had tried understanding each team member’s individual drives, and suggest one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood. Harold said he would try it, thanked Arthur, and felt more hopeful.
- Harold then implemented one-on-one chats with his team. He told them he wanted quick one-on-one conversations to understand what motivated each of them, believing it would help them work better together. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them and urged them to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future, so he discussed alternative strategies with Arthur.
- In their second meeting, Harold told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding well and he was worried. He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper. Harold said he would set up another round of meetings to get to the bottom of it.
- Harold then held more one-on-one meetings. He told team members he had noticed performance issues and wanted to understand their concerns. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few people that was affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload, stressed, and had difficulty staying motivated. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important to him.
- Afterward, Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He told the team he wanted to create a more supportive environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said their input and well-being were crucial and encouraged them to work together.

Harold does not know the private thoughts, hidden motives, or unspoken information of Arthur or the team members beyond what they said or what he observed. He also does not know narrator-only facts such as others’ personality types or internal reasoning.
